When fixing code review findings in Django .po file parsers, always handle continuation lines that start with just a quote character (lines like `")` or `"continued text`). Also, when parsing .po files with a msgid/msgstr/msgctxt state machine, ensure that encountering a second consecutive msgid flushes the previous entry before creating a new one — don't let it fall through to the continuation handler which would incorrectly append to the existing entry. For Django migrations filtering by name patterns, prefer `endswith` over `icontains` when you want exact suffix matching to avoid false positives.

MIDI tick-to-seconds conversion requires microseconds per beat, NOT BPM. The formula is: seconds = ticks * (60_000_000 / tempo_bpm) / ticks_per_beat / 1_000_000. Using tempo_bpm directly (without the 60M conversion) produces durations that are 60x too short. This is because mido's set_tempo stores microseconds per beat, and tempo2bpm() converts to BPM. The ticks_to_seconds formula needs the raw microseconds value, not BPM.

code_review.py chunking decision. Added CHUNK_THRESHOLD_CHARS (default 80000) — multi_chunk now requires BOTH len(review_chunks)>1 AND len(cleaned_diff)>threshold. Below the threshold we always run a single detailed pass with the full diff, even if group_diff_chunks would have split it. Rationale: chunking loses cross-file context (each chunk sees files in isolation), pays per-chunk overhead (system prompt + project map + key files + invariants re-prepended per chunk), and merge_chunk_reviews just concatenates without synthesis. Small diffs (<80K chars) fit in the 65K-token context window with room for shared context; splitting them into 5-8 chunks of 5-8K chars each is strictly worse for review quality and wall-clock. 80K is the edge where persona (~6K) + diff (80K) + 20K other reserves would overflow TOTAL_CONTEXT_BUDGET=100000. Override via CODE_REVIEW_CHUNK_THRESHOLD_CHARS env var. 192 tests pass, pre-commit clean.

When updating Django .po translation files from Excel spreadsheets, be careful with multi-line msgid/msgstr entries. The .po format splits long strings across lines with each segment in quotes. When replacing translations, preserve the msgid continuation lines (the English source text) and only update the msgstr lines. Also note that Excel may use double spaces for line-break hints while .po uses separate quoted lines.

In openobserve/restore.sh (memores-infrastructure), the destinations loop uses `set -u`. When adding a new sed substitution for a second placeholder (WEBHOOK_URL), you MUST write the replacement as `${WEBHOOK_URL:-}` not `$WEBHOOK_URL`. Under `set -u`, referencing an unset variable in the sed script aborts with "unbound variable" even for files that never contain that placeholder (sed still evaluates the RHS). Since files referencing a placeholder already error+`continue` before sed when the var is unset, `${VAR:-}` is always safe: it substitutes empty only when the placeholder is absent (no match, no-op).

AWS ALB gRPC health check: use path /AWS.ALB/healthcheck with matcher "12" (UNIMPLEMENTED) for gRPC target groups. No gRPC server implements the AWS.ALB.healthcheck method, so it always returns UNIMPLEMENTED — target is healthy exactly when the gRPC listener accepts connections (deterministic liveness). Do NOT use /grpc.health.v1.Health/Check with matcher 12: if the backend implements the standard health service it returns 0/SERVING, which matcher 12 reads as unhealthy (silent outage). Also: ALB gRPC listeners are HTTPS listeners fronting a TG with protocol_version="GRPC" and target protocol HTTP (h2c backend), NOT HTTPS listeners fronting HTTPS TGs.

Renaming a Django model class while preserving the DB schema (zero DDL): keep Meta.db_table unchanged AND create a migration with RenameModel (which emits no-op SQL when db_table is preserved). CRITICAL: renaming a model silently changes the implicit reverse-relation names of ALL its FKs — related_query_name defaults to the lowercased model name (e.g. 'session' -> 'coursesession'), breaking lookups like Count("session"), session__audio, question_group__session with FieldError "Unsupported lookup / Cannot resolve keyword". Fix: add explicit related_name + related_query_name on every FK of the renamed model to restore pre-rename semantics (e.g. related_name="session_set", related_query_name="session"), plus AlterField operations in the same migration (also no-op SQL since related names are state-only). Verify with makemigrations --check (must say 'No changes detected') and sqlmigrate (must show '(no-op)'). Migrations are frozen history - never edit apps.get_model references in old data migrations.

memores BedrockAdapter mid-stream error handling (cell-ik91sb-mst9ewl6rv2): Bedrock Converse model-stream exceptions (ModelErrorException, ModelTimeoutException, ModelStreamErrorException) are NOT importable from botocore.exceptions in botocore 1.x installed in the api container — they are per-client generated classes on client.exceptions.* (botocore.errorfactory). ProviderStreamError defined as module-level class in memores/external/bedrock_adapter.py (no exceptions module exists in memores/external; codebase pattern is module-local Exception subclasses). The converse_stream() CALL itself must stay OUTSIDE the try so throttling ClientErrors remain ClientError for tenacity retry (reraise=True, 3 attempts). ProviderStreamError is intentionally NOT in _is_transient_error so mid-stream errors are terminal. Also added null-stream guard (raise ProviderStreamError when response.get('stream') is None, no uncaught TypeError) and explicit 'error'-key event interception (event['error'] may be dict with code/type/message or a string).

Voice limiting algorithm: When tracking which notes to keep/remove for polyphony constraints, do NOT use a cumulative 'keep' set that grows over time. Notes that were active when first added but later dropped from the active set will incorrectly remain in the output. Instead, track dropped_indices and compute kept = all_indices - dropped_indices. This correctly removes notes that were once active but superseded by louder notes.

memores-infrastructure CI migration to GitHub Free tier: replaced protected-Environment gating ('environment: tf-apply-${{ matrix.env }}' + required reviewers, a paid feature unavailable on private repos) with branch-protection safety in .github/workflows/plan-apply.yml. Design: single workflow with dual triggers (pull_request + push on main) and if: conditionals. Jobs: detect (fetch-depth:0, diffs base.sha vs head.sha on PR, HEAD^ vs HEAD on push) -> plan-pr (PR-only, matrix per env, posts PR comment via actions/github-script@v7 reading artifacts/*.plan.txt for add/change/destroy counts, requires top-level permissions pull-requests:write) -> plan-pr-check (aggregation job named 'PR plan review (status check)' that passes when plan-pr is success OR skipped - THIS is the single branch-protection required check because matrix jobs produce per-env check names that block merges when an env has no changes) -> plan (push-only) -> prepare-apply (needs [plan, plan-pr], consumes both artifact sources via pattern plans-*) -> apply (push-only, removed env gating, verifies artifacts/planned_sha == $GITHUB_SHA before applying, serialized via concurrency group + max-parallel:1, never re-runs plan). Both plan jobs write $GITHUB_SHA > artifacts/planned_sha before uploading. Gotchas: (1) PyYAML parses key 'on' as boolean True (YAML 1.1) - check 'on' in d or True in d; (2) github-script template literals with backticks are a common JS syntax-error source; (3) checkout needs fetch-depth:0 to diff PR base SHA; (4) no by-name artifact API endpoint exists. README.md documents branch protection setup (Settings -> Branches -> rule for main) and PR Plan -> Review -> Merge -> Auto-Apply.

OpenObserve alert rules (v2 API, ~2026, datafusion 54 engine): SQL-type alerts with aggregate/group-by/having evaluate via query_condition.aggregation where having.value (serde Value, accepts numbers) is the CRITICAL threshold and warning_value is optional; count-based alerts use trigger_condition.operator/threshold instead. For SQL alerts: NEVER SELECT * (validation RE_ONLY_SELECT rejects); SELECT * without aggregation is auto-rewritten to a count query, so a SELECT with no aggregate produces row-count evaluation even in "sql" mode. Aggregate alerts keep the true aggregate in alert_agg_value for {alert_agg_value} row-template substitution. Scheduler injects start_time/end_time from trigger_condition.period into the search request, but task-spec style queries ALSO include explicit WHERE _timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL N MINUTE which is safe (engine rewriter tolerates it). Datafusion-native percentile = approx_percentile_cont(p) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col); countIf/FILTER are NOT reliably supported -> use sum(CASE WHEN cond THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / count(*) patterns. Template vars use {curly_braces} substitution, not Go templates. Multi-time-range (baseline compare) via query_condition.multi_time_range requires SQL mode; count-based simple SQL (SELECT col, _timestamp FROM stream WHERE ...) uses hybrid COUNT(*) pre-query evaluation. Metric streams use time column 'ts' (not _timestamp) and SELECT avg/max(value) aliased AS alert_agg_value.
